### Target Branch

0.88

### Link to commit or PR to be picked

- https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/58398
- https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/58446

### Description

Requesting the React 19.3.0 sync for the 0.88 release. Please pick the commits in this order:

1. `73a76ddced2088d925809432fd6b0503f239dbfe` (#58398)
2. `b0b71421c1964e046ba2ad156669c7d32e4c538f` (#58446)

#58398 is a required runtime prerequisite that is not present on `0.88-stable`. The React 19.3 Fabric renderer imports `react-native/react-private-interface` and dereferences `fabricUIManager` during module initialization. Without #58398, that property is undefined and renderer initialization fails. The prerequisite exposes the existing Fabric UIManager proxy through the private interface.

I reviewed the contiguous commits after the sync on `main`. None is a corrective fix required by the React 19.3 update:

- #58447 only enables previously guarded Fantom tests.
- #58450 separately enables EventTarget-based event dispatch by default; the synced renderer retains the legacy path, so this behavior rollout is not required for correctness.
- #58399, #58452, #58454, and #58455 remove bindings, forwarding modules, globals, and getters that the new renderer no longer consumes.

I also reviewed #58443, which landed before the sync. It aligns the FabricUIManager Flow interface and cached-property list with the native binding, but it is not a runtime prerequisite: the existing proxy explicitly falls back to the original native object for uncached properties, and the 0.88 native binding already provides the methods used by the new renderer.

A three-way application check against current `origin/0.88-stable` shows #58398 applying cleanly. The sync has expected content conflicts only in `packages/rn-tester/package.json` and `private/helloworld/package.json`, where the release branch contains `0.88.0-rc.0` version stamps and `main` contains development versions. The React 19.3 dependency updates should be applied while retaining the 0.88 release version stamps.

### Target Branch

0.88

### Link to commit or PR to be picked

https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/58518

### Description

`findFilesWithExtension` walks a library's directory looking for `.mm` files that declare a Fabric component. The walk descends into every subdirectory, `node_modules` included, resolves symlinks through `statSync`, and keeps no visited set.

This got broken after https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/57790 because `parseiOSAnnotations` now enters every library that declares a `codegenConfig` without an `ios` key into its map with an empty `components` object, so nothing removes it from `librariesToCrawl`. Previously such libraries were filtered before crawling. 

An app that declares `codegenConfig` with `"type": "all"` and no `ios` key now gets treated as a component library, so the walk covers the entire project.

### Target Branch

0.88

### Link to commit or PR to be picked

- https://github.com/react-native-community/template/pull/249 (commit `aad5b40ded3933a66166c11fe05835467bba48a3`)

### Description

Note this is a pick in `react-native-community/template`, not in `react/react-native`. Opening it here for bookkeeping so the 0.88 pick list is complete.

The React 19.3.0 sync (#1408, https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/58446) has been picked into `0.88-stable`. That commit bumps the `react-native` package's peer dependency:

```
"peerDependencies": {
-   "react": "^19.2.3"
+   "react": "^19.3.0"
}
```

The `0.88-stable` branch of `react-native-community/template` still pins `react: 19.2.3`, so the generated app and the picked `react-native` no longer agree. `test_e2e_ios_templateapp` and `test_e2e_android_templateapp` now fail in all four configurations (Debug and Release on both platforms) while installing the scaffolded project:

```
npm error code ERESOLVE
npm error While resolving: RNTestProject@0.0.1
npm error Found: react@19.2.3
npm error   react@"19.2.3" from the root project
npm error Could not resolve dependency:
npm error peer react@"^19.3.0" from react-native@0.88.0-rc.0
```

Failing run: https://github.com/react/react-native/actions/runs/34846501953

`scripts/e2e/init-project-e2e.js` clones the template repo, checks out the branch matching the current release branch, then rewrites only the `@react-native/*` scoped dependencies and `react-native` itself. It never rewrites `react`, so the pin has to be correct on the template's release branch.

Both halves of this change already landed on `main` on the same day:

| Repo | Change | Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `react/react-native` | #58446 React 19.3.0 sync | 2026-09-10 |
| `react-native-community/template` | #249 Update react and react-test-renderer to 19.3.0 | 2026-09-10 |

The template's `0.88-stable` branch was cut on 2026-09-08, two days before #249, and has not been updated since, so it missed the bump. Only the `react/react-native` half was picked into 0.88.

The pick is two lines in `template/package.json`:

```diff
-    "react": "19.2.3",
+    "react": "19.3.0",
...
-    "react-test-renderer": "19.2.3",
+    "react-test-renderer": "19.3.0",
```

Note that `react-native` on the template's `main` is pinned to `nightly` while the release branch pins the release version, so only the two `react` lines should be taken.

This is a required follow-up to the React 19.3.0 sync rather than an independent change. Without it the template e2e jobs cannot pass on `0.88-stable`, and anyone scaffolding a new app from the 0.88 template hits the same peer dependency conflict.

### Target Branch

0.88

### Link to commit or PR to be picked

- https://github.com/facebook/hermes/pull/1988 (the source backport, 10 of its commits)

### Description

Bookkeeping record. **All 10 commits have already landed on `260318099.0.0-stable`, so there is nothing to action here.** Filing it so the 0.88 pick list reflects the work, and so the remaining release-side blocker is written down somewhere.

#### The gap

RN 0.88 moved to Hermes `260318099`, whose stable branch was cut from `static_h` around 2026-03-18. https://github.com/facebook/hermes/pull/1988 ("Backport new JSI improvements", 21 commits from `static_h`) landed on the `250829098` branch (used by RN 0.87) on 2026-04-15, after that cut.

The `260318099` branch received only half of it. The **JSI declarations** ("Add `X` API") crossed over, the **Hermes implementations** ("Implement `X`") and their SynthTrace support did not. The JSI surface in `API/jsi/jsi/jsi.h` was byte-identical between the two branches, so nothing failed to compile and nothing raised an error. Every affected API silently fell through to the `jsi` base implementation.

This was found through `tryGetMutableBuffer`, where `expo-modules-core`'s Android instrumentation tests caught the zero-copy regression on 0.88.0-rc.0 (https://github.com/expo/expo/pull/49910). The other five APIs had the same defect and were latent.

#### Where each commit landed

| # | Source (`250829098.0.0-stable`) | API | Landed on `260318099.0.0-stable` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `d44b213d74f` | `Array.push` impl | `9841318e1` |
| 2 | `f5ce8f0e586` | `Array.push` SynthTrace | `2daaa8aa8` |
| 3 | `9a50bd0f364` | `tryGetMutableBuffer` impl | `ccb4fb5bd` (via facebook/hermes#2179) |
| 4 | `5d5c9334bec` | `getMutableBuffer` SynthTrace | `41ed32d43` |
| 5 | `93eee4c7e4c` | `ArrayBuffer.detached` impl | `fd3724fb1` |
| 6 | `1aea879f113` | `createUInt8Array` impl | `7b15bccd7` |
| 7 | `9d28826712c` | `createUInt8Array`, `TypedArray::buffer` SynthTrace | `c926dd7a1` |
| 8 | `5b31237bf83` | Error creation impl | `5d1e7237d` |
| 9 | `e6268f9dee7` | Error creation SynthTrace | `1b374ae69` |
| 10 | `5a7f83aa3a1` | `String::length` impl | `7e5dfcd59` |

Nine landed as `Graft "[SH] ..." to shermes/stable`. Number 3 landed through facebook/hermes#2179.

Verified by content rather than by commit subject. Every `HermesRuntimeImpl` method (`push`, `tryGetMutableBuffer`, `detached`, `createUint8Array`, `isTypedArray`, `createError`, `createRangeError`, `createSyntaxError`, `length`) is now present in `API/hermes/hermes.cpp` on the 0.88 branch, and `API/hermes/TracingRuntime.cpp` matches the 0.87 branch exactly (4 / 1 / 2 occurrences of `createUint8Array` / `tryGetMutableBuffer` / `createError`, against 0 / 0 / 0 before).

#### Still outstanding, and this is the part that affects the release

**There is no `260318099.0.3` tag.** Tags stop at `hermes-v260318099.0.2`, and RN `0.88-stable` pins `260318099.0.2` in `packages/react-native/sdks/hermes-engine/version.properties` and `packages/react-native/package.json`. None of the work above reaches the release until a new tag is cut and RN is bumped to it.

Three separate things are waiting on that tag:

1. This batch of 10 commits.
2. The back-out of the VariableScope rescan pick (facebook/hermes#2149). `hermes-v260318099.0.2` was tagged at 2026-09-08 03:05 PDT and the back-out landed at 11:18 PDT the same day, so `.0.2` still carries the change that was reverted for causing SIGSEGV crashes in Messenger Android (D118959426).
3. `xplat/static_h` still carries that same change (`maybeDeadVariableScopes_` is still present in `lib/IR/IR.cpp` on `static_h`). The back-out called this out as a follow-up that was not included, since `static_h` is the source the next `stable` sync pulls from.

Closing as landed.

content.body:
### Target Branch

0.88

### Link to commit or PR to be picked

Pick in this order (oldest first):

1. https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/58290 — `1cfc5f29a00` — Derive an SPM library's Swift name from its podspec
2. https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/58362 — `25f48bd72fd` — Run SPM-generated shell scripts under bash, not `/bin/sh`
3. https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/58379 — `92564f33fda` — Derive the generated manifests' iOS platform floor from the app (D119653699)

### Description

The change we actually want is #58379. The other two are prerequisites, so the request covers all three.

#### Why #58379 is needed

The SwiftPM manifests React Native generates (the `Autolinked` aggregate, the per-dependency synth packages and the scaffolded community packages) hardcode `platforms: [.iOS(.v15)]`. SwiftPM refuses to link a product whose minimum platform is above the depending target's, so any self-managed package with a higher floor cannot be autolinked.

Every Expo package declares iOS 16.4, so a stock Expo app fails at build time:

```
error: The package product 'Expo' requires minimum platform version 16.4 for the iOS platform,
       but this target supports 15.0 (in target 'AutolinkedAggregate' from project 'Autolinked')
```

The app itself is correct (`IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 16.4`). Only the generated manifests disagree. The fix derives the floor from the app's own deployment target, clamped to React Native's minimum (15.1).

#### Why the prerequisites

**#58290 is a hard dependency.** #58379 imports `findPodspecs` and `readPodspecCached` from `scripts/spm/read-podspec.js`. On `0.88-stable` that module exports only `readPodspec`, so the pick does not build without #58290 first. Cherry-picking #58379 alone conflicts in `generate-spm-autolinking.js` and `scaffold-package-swift.js`.

**#58362 is taken to avoid a conflict.** It and #58379 both modify `scripts/spm/generate-spm-xcodeproj.js`. Not a functional dependency, but skipping it makes #58379 conflict there.

**#58425 is deliberately not taken.** It is chronologically between #58362 and #58379 and touches `scripts/spm/`, but shares no file with #58379 (it changes `download-spm-artifacts.js`, the CocoaPods ruby helpers and the Gradle Kotlin plugin). It is a separate concern and is not required here.

#### Risk

The chain is larger than a typical post-RC1 pick, so worth being explicit about the blast radius.

All of the code these commits change lives under `packages/react-native/scripts/spm/` plus `scripts/setup-apple-spm.js`. That tree is required only by `setup-apple-spm.js`, which is a manual entry point (`node node_modules/react-native/scripts/setup-apple-spm.js [action]`). It is not wired into `pod install` or any build phase. The only SPM code that runs unconditionally is the CocoaPods hook `SPM.apply_on_post_install`, which iterates a dependency map that stays empty unless a podspec declares an SPM dependency, and none of these commits touch it.

So an app that does not opt into SwiftPM cannot execute a line any of these change.

The remaining files in #58290 are `packages/rn-tester/` and `packages/react-native-test-library/`, which are React Native's own fixtures and are not shipped.

On size: #58290 reads as +3386/-912 across 26 files, but roughly 2264 of those additions are test files and ~143 are docs. The production delta is around +900/-325.

Two behaviour changes that do land, both only for SwiftPM users:

- SwiftPM name collisions become a hard error naming `swiftpmConfig.name` as the fix, where previously colliding names were auto-corrected. The old behaviour invented a module name no `#import` could predict, so the error is the better outcome, but it is new.
- `SCAFFOLDER_VERSION` bumps to 20, so existing scaffolds regenerate with the new floor on the next `spm add` / `spm update`.

#### Prerequisite audit

Checked against a full (unshallowed) `main` history: every SPM commit preceding #58290 is already on `0.88-stable` (#58292, #58060, #58044, #58033, #58087, #58059, #58034, #58035). The chain starts cleanly at #58290 and is exactly these three.
content.title: [0.88] [iOS][SPM] Derive the generated manifests' iOS platform floor from the app (+2 prerequisites)

content.body:
### Target Branch

0.88

### Link to commit or PR to be picked

- https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/57513 (the change being corrected)
- Fix applied directly to `0.88-stable` as `579212e15c9`

### Description

Bookkeeping record. **This is a `0.88-stable`-only fix with no corresponding commit on `main`,** so there is nothing to pick. Filing it so the 0.88 list is complete and so the deliberate divergence from `main` is written down.

#### The regression

#57513 relocated the hand-written `.d.ts` declarations under `types_DEPRECATED/` and updated the `exports` map. It describes itself as "a pure relocation with no change to the public type surface".

For `./Libraries/*`, the `react-native-legacy-deep-imports` condition changed:

| | resolves to |
| --- | --- |
| 0.87 | `./Libraries/*.d.ts` |
| 0.88 | `./types_DEPRECATED/Libraries/*.d.ts` |

On 0.87 that target sat beside the real `.js`, so TypeScript's extension substitution still found modules that have no hand-written declaration. `types_DEPRECATED/` contains no `.js` files at all, so on 0.88 those specifiers stop resolving. `types_DEPRECATED/Libraries/` has 83 declarations; `Libraries/` has 619 `.js` modules.

Reported by @gabrieldonadel against 0.88.0-rc.0. Reproduced against the published packages with a tsconfig setting `customConditions` to `["react-native", "react-native-legacy-deep-imports"]` and importing `react-native/Libraries/Core/InitializeCore`:

```
react-native@0.87.1       tsc exit 0
react-native@0.88.0-rc.1  tsc exit 2
  TS2882: Cannot find module or type declarations for side-effect import
```

This is not framework-only. The condition is the documented escape hatch: `@react-native/typescript-config`'s README instructs consumers to set it, and `packages/virtualized-lists` uses it.

#### The fix

```diff
 "./Libraries/*": {
-  "react-native-legacy-deep-imports": "./types_DEPRECATED/Libraries/*.d.ts",
+  "react-native-legacy-deep-imports": [
+    "./types_DEPRECATED/Libraries/*.d.ts",
+    "./Libraries/*.d.ts"
+  ],
   "types": null,
   "default": "./Libraries/*.js"
 },
```

Verified:

- The failing import resolves again.
- Modules that do have a declaration are unaffected, since that entry is still first. `registerCallableModule` keeps its real declaration and a deliberately invalid call still errors rather than passing as `any`.
- A value import from an untyped module (`Libraries/Utilities/logError`) produces the identical `TS7016` implicit-any diagnostic as 0.87.1, so this restores parity rather than adding new `any` leakage.
- Passes with `moduleResolution` set to `bundler`, `node16` and `nodenext`.
- Runtime resolution is unchanged. Without the custom condition, Node still resolves via `default` to the real `.js`.
- `yarn test-typescript-legacy` passes.

Not fixed, and not a regression: `react-native/Libraries/Core/InitializeCore.js` with an explicit `.js` suffix also fails on 0.87.1. The `./Libraries/*.js` subpath carries no legacy condition on either branch.

#### Why this is not on `main`

Deliberate. 0.88 is a non-breaking release, so the regression must not ship in it. `main` keeps the current behaviour for now because retiring deep imports is the direction of [RFC0894](https://github.com/react-native-community/discussions-and-proposals/pull/894) and 0.89 is a breaking release, which is the right window for it.

Worth flagging for whoever picks this up: `main` is currently in a half-broken state rather than a cleanly retired one. The escape hatch resolves for the 83 modules with a declaration and fails with a bare `TS2882` for the rest, with no deprecation warning, changelog entry or migration guidance. If deep imports are to be retired in 0.89, removing the condition outright with a changelog entry would give consumers a clearer signal than leaving resolution to fail arbitrarily.

A diff applying the same fix to `main` exists but is intentionally not landed, pending that decision.
content.title: [0.88] Restore .js fallback for legacy deep imports of untyped modules (regression from #57513)

content.body:
### Target Branch

0.88

### Link to commit or PR to be picked

Reverts, both on `0.88-stable`:

- https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/57879 (`11f9a7f4491`) — RCTArrayBuffer zero-copy class for ObjC TM
- https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/57596 (`5e86c323cef`) — Use NSData for the JS->ObjC ArrayBuffer argument path

### Description

0.88 is a **non-breaking** release. #57879 is a confirmed breaking change to the ObjC TurboModule surface and must not ship in it.

#### The breaking change

Codegen emits a different ObjC type for TurboModule methods taking or returning an `ArrayBuffer`. Modules that adopted ObjC `ArrayBuffer` support in 0.87 stop compiling until they update. It is already documented in the 0.88.0-rc.0 changelog under `Breaking`.

#### Why two reverts and not one

The type moved **twice inside 0.88**, so reverting #57879 alone does not restore 0.87:

| Point | Argument type | Return type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.87-stable | `NSMutableData *` | `NSMutableData *` |
| after #57596 (0.88 only) | `NSMutableData *` | **`NSData *`** |
| after #57879 (0.88 only) | `RCTArrayBuffer *` | `RCTArrayBuffer *` |

`NSMutableData` is a subclass of `NSData`, so returning `NSData` where 0.87 returned `NSMutableData` still breaks any caller that mutates the result. Reverting only #57879 would leave a second, quieter breaking change in place.

#### Scope, and how it was determined

Enumerated every 0.88-only commit touching the ObjC TurboModule surface (codegen `GenerateModuleObjCpp`, `RCTArrayBuffer.*`, the iOS `ReactCommon` module dir, `iostests`, and the Apple cxx-api snapshots), then filtered to those whose added or removed lines mention `ArrayBuffer`, `NSData` or `NSMutableData`. Five matched:

- `11f9a7f4491` #57879 — **revert**
- `5e86c323cef` #57596 — **revert**
- `d84c13d5111` #57982, `5bb96395949` #57897 — Java only, Android snapshots, zero ObjC codegen type changes
- `5fb3ebce1ac` — Java ArrayBuffer support. Touches the ObjC codegen, but only to add the `throwIfUnsupportedPromiseArrayBuffer` validation guard. No type mapping, so out of scope.

All four `RCTArrayBuffer` entries in the public Apple API snapshot blame to `11f9a7f4491` alone.

#### Kept, not reverted

- https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/58264 (`253a84c8d1c`) — TurboModule identity on rethrown exceptions
- https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/58190 (`ea291d7422e`) — top-level JS null to ObjC as `nil`

Both conflict with the revert, but each references `RCTArrayBuffer` **only in context lines**, never in an added or removed line. The conflicts are textual adjacency, not a dependency, so both were preserved through hand-resolution.

- https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/57518 (`e7bb11ae162`) — also kept. It adds one `#import <react/bridging/ArrayBuffer.h>` line. After the reverts, `RCTTurboModuleArrayBufferTests.mm` is byte-identical to 0.87 apart from that import, and the header exists on 0.87.

#### Verification

- Resolved codegen `serializeMethod.js` ArrayBuffer lines are identical to 0.87-stable.
- Regenerated `GenerateModuleHObjCpp` snapshot matches 0.87 except for `promiseArrayBuffer`, which the `throwIfUnsupportedPromiseArrayBuffer` guard now rejects. That guard is a separate 0.88 change, deliberately retained.
- No `RCTArrayBuffer` or `mustCopyBytes` references remain anywhere under `ReactCommon/react/nativemodule/`.
- `convertJSIValueToObjCObject` is back to its 4-parameter form with `BOOL useNSNull = NO` defaulted in the header, so the restored 3-argument call sites compile.
- The three #58190 tests and the #58264 test are all still present.
- `yarn jest packages/react-native-codegen` passes: 64 suites, 3129 tests, 1279 snapshots.

Net: 16 files, 132 insertions, 607 deletions.

The iOS build and the ObjC unit tests are covered by branch CI rather than locally.
content.title: [0.88] Revert RCTArrayBuffer ObjC TurboModule type change (breaking in a non-breaking release)

content.body:
### Target Branch

0.88

### Link to commit or PR to be picked

Revert of https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/58063 (`ab2ea649e65`) on `0.88-stable`.

### Description

0.88 is a **non-breaking** release. #58063 is a confirmed breaking change for C++ TurboModules and must not ship in it.

#### What it does

It adds a codegen parse-time guard, `throwIfEventEmitterPayloadTypeIsUnsupported`, that rejects `ArrayBuffer` as a TurboModule `EventEmitter` payload on all platforms:

```js
export interface Spec extends TurboModule {
  +onBuffer: EventEmitter<ArrayBuffer>;
}
```

#### Why this is breaking, demonstrated

The same spec was run through both branches' codegen. It worked on 0.87 and is rejected on 0.88:

| | 0.87.1 | 0.88-stable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parse | accepted | **rejected** |
| `GenerateModuleH` (`modulesCxx`) | **succeeded** | never runs |
| `GenerateModuleObjCpp` | threw, "Unsupported eventType" | never runs |

The C++ output on 0.87 is functional, not placeholder:

```cpp
eventEmitterMap_["onBuffer"] = std::make_shared<AsyncEventEmitter<jsi::Value>>();
static_assert(bridging::supportsFromJs<OnBufferType, jsi::ArrayBuffer>, ...);
static_cast<AsyncEventEmitter<jsi::Value>&>(*eventEmitterMap_["onBuffer"]).emit(...)
```

and the `static_assert` passes on 0.87, because `struct Bridging<jsi::ArrayBuffer>` with `fromJs` and `toJs` exists at `react/bridging/ArrayBuffer.h:46` and is exported through the `Bridging.h` umbrella. `modulesCxx` is a consumer-facing codegen target.

So a C++ TurboModule with an ArrayBuffer event payload parsed, generated, compiled and had working bridging on 0.87, and its build fails on 0.88 with no code change by the consumer.

The iOS path already rejected it on 0.87, which is why this needed checking per generator target rather than once.

#### Scope

Surface: the codegen parser and generator files that implement the guard (`error-utils.js`, `errors.js`, `parsers-commons.js`, `generators/modules/Utils.js`, `GenerateModuleH.js`, `GenerateModuleJavaSpec.js`, `GenerateModuleObjCpp/serializeEventEmitter.js`).

0.88-only commits touching that surface, baseline `v0.87.1`:

- `ab2ea649e65` #58063 — **revert**
- `5bb96395949` #57897, `4bf55754905`, `5fb3ebce1ac` — all predate it and add **zero** EventEmitter payload validation

Nothing lands after `ab2ea649e65` on those files, so no later work conflicts. Both symbols it introduced (`throwIfEventEmitterPayloadTypeIsUnsupported`, `UnsupportedModuleEventEmitterPayloadTypeParserError`) are referenced only by files that commit itself created or modified, so the revert is self-contained.

Single commit. 23 files, all JavaScript under `react-native-codegen`, no native code.

#### Not reverted

`d84c13d5111` (#57982, Java ArrayBuffer borrow contract) is annotated `[Android][Breaking]` but is **not breaking for this release**. All three Java ArrayBuffer TurboModule commits are 0.88-only, and 0.87's Android API snapshot contains no Java-facing ArrayBuffer type, only the C++ `facebook::jsi::ArrayBuffer` and `facebook::react::AsyncArrayBuffer`. No 0.87 consumer could have adopted it, so constraining it in 0.88 breaks nobody. The label is correct against `main`'s history, not against the released line.

#### Verification

- Revert applies cleanly, no conflicts.
- After reverting, the same spec behaves **identically to 0.87**: parse accepted, `GenerateModuleH` succeeds, `GenerateModuleObjCpp` throws "Unsupported eventType".
- Both introduced symbols are gone from the tree.
- `yarn jest packages/react-native-codegen` passes: 64 suites, 3122 tests, 1277 snapshots.
content.title: [0.88] Revert EventEmitter ArrayBuffer payload rejection (breaking for C++ TurboModules)

### Note: retroactive record

Backfilled alongside #1419 so the 0.88 series has the reports the process requires. Per [the testing guide](https://github.com/reactwg/react-native-releases/blob/main/docs/guide-release-testing.md), manual testing is required for **RC0, RC1, the golden RC and stable**, so rc.1 needs one as well as rc.0. The four dimensions are recorded as covered per the release captain; per-case notes and system configuration from the original session were not captured.

### What shipped in rc.1

12 commits between the two tags, notably the React 19.3.0 sync (#58446), the EventTarget dispatch work (#58450, #58479), the SPM chain (#58290, #58362, #58379), the codegen crawl fix (#58518) and the Hermes bump to `260318099.0.3`.

### CI state on the release commit

`Test All` was green on the `v0.88.0-rc.1` commit apart from the known `test_js` failure, which was the same structural `cache-key-test.js` problem described in #1419 and was fixed later that day in `ad7b17d8eef`.

Two template e2e issues were found and resolved during this RC rather than after it:

- the template's `react` pin lagged the 19.3.0 sync, causing `ERESOLVE` across all four template e2e jobs. Fixed in `react-native-community/template` on its `0.88-stable` branch, which the e2e clones at run time, so a rerun picked it up with no RN commit needed.
- `post_publish` failed on its 3-minute "Verify Release is on NPM" timeout. The publish itself succeeded; this is npm propagation lag, not a release failure.
